observations: The top of Most Popular is unchanged: Steal An Egg (89 days) leads ahead of evergreens Brookhaven, Murder Mystery 2, RIVALS and 99 Nights in the Forest.
Multi-year games hold a median pillar percentile of 65 against 37–43 for games under a year, so age still separates staying power.
The biggest risers are young: Bike Universe +29 (25 days), Ride a Dino +21, Eat Everything In A Grocery Store +19 (19 days) and Fake an Egg +12 (18 days).
Four games entered, including Clone Baby Care (Anomaly) at 13 days and DIVINE HATCHERS, while WRONG WAY! and Piggy fell off.
Games left more than about 9 days without an update stay on the chart for fewer days (rho -0.34), which keeps H-mp-018 at 65%.
patterns: Multiplayer loops (PvP combat, roleplay, co-op survival) consistently rank above solo loops; idle tycoons (13th percentile) and +1 incrementals (33rd) sit lowest.
Higher median pass and product prices go with longer presence (product median above 499 R$ r=+0.41). Part of this is age: older games carry deeper price ladders.
Egg and RP title words go with better positions, while Soccer titles go with worse. The Egg effect is mostly Steal An Egg and its clones.
Video observations of long-running hits show low-HUD social worlds (Brookhaven, Adopt Me!) next to dense-HUD progression games (Blox Fruits), so HUD density alone doesn't explain staying power.

outliers.name: Steal An Egg
outliers.note: A template steal/egg game at 89 days holding #1 against multi-year evergreens; its early lead and constant updates appear to have kept it ahead of its own clones.

outliers.name: +1 Speed Keyboard Escape | Candy & Chocolate
outliers.note: A solo +1 incremental near the top, against the solo-loop pattern; 46 passes and 205 products suggest deep monetization and frequent world updates keep it there.

observations: Donation and social hubs (Summer Donations, Donation Central, Simple DONATIONS) again top monetization efficiency, followed by Elemental Dungeons and Spin a KPOP Idol.
Efficiency keeps rising with age: median percentile 23 at 15–42 days, 43 at 43–84 days, 58 for games past a year.
The weakest are young simulators with large audiences that haven't monetized yet (a 19-day Arabic hunting game, Climb For Animals Eggs, Cat Battles).
The chart was stable today: no notable risers, fallers or entries in the scored set.
patterns: Median developer product price above 79 R$ consistently goes with higher efficiency (r=+0.40 at the split). This is the strongest page-level lever.
RPGs (r=+0.46), roleplay hubs (r=+0.30) and PvP combat consistently earn more per player, while Simulation, Survival, steal/defend and pet/egg loops earn less.
Complexity, longer descriptions, bigger servers and caps-heavy, update-tagged titles all go with efficiency. Game age is a likely shared confounder for all of them.
Reward-flex thumbnails go with lower efficiency (r=-0.21), consistent with big-number simulators earning less per player.

outliers.name: [🎃] Spin a KPOP Idol
outliers.note: A solo simulator in the top efficiency group, against both the solo and Simulation patterns; its gacha spins on a licensed-feel K-pop theme likely carry high spending per player.

outliers.name: [CURE] Violence District
outliers.note: An old survival game with only 2 passes and 20 products sits among the weakest; few things to buy limit its revenue despite a large audience.

observations: DONT SPLASH (5 days) leads momentum at +25, followed by Something is Wrong With My Dog... +23, +1 Dance Battle Evolution +22, Where Is Fahd? +19 and Escooter Life +18.
The youngest games carry the most momentum: 0–14 days median percentile 81 against 44 at 43–84 days, consistent with H-tt-001.
Thirteen games entered, including It Hears The Water (8 days), Make a Pancake!, Clean the House! and Feed the Fire; 13 fell off, including Paint a Pancake and Break and Steal an Egg.
Older re-surfacing games (Murder Mystery 2, Wanted, Kayak and Surf) also entered, likely carried by Halloween updates.
patterns: Launching with more than 8 game passes tends to go with lower positions (within-age -0.34), and generic 2x passes tend to as well.
Horror, co-op survival and story-adventure loops sit at the top of momentum (median percentiles 97, 87, 81), while simulation jobs and obbies lag.
Young games with drivable vehicles may hold higher positions (r=+0.40); bike, scooter and rally games are a visible share of entries. A new test is added today.
Games with a collection index tend to hold higher positions (within-age +0.58), though the count is small.

outliers.name: Something is Wrong With My Dog...
outliers.note: At 57 days, beyond the 6-week fade, it still climbs +23; it adapts a viral indie horror concept, which may bring its own audience.

outliers.name: Crazy Diver
outliers.note: A 55% like ratio but strong momentum, so curiosity-driven physics clips may beat quality signals early.

observations: DONT SPLASH, Bike Universe, Clone Baby Care (Anomaly), Steel Fighters, Backseat Rally and Fix My Phone! hold the top of Up-and-Coming.
Thirteen games entered: three horror/anomaly games (It Hears The Water, Anomaly Party, Airport Security), Steal A DNA, Create a Robot Fighter, Bullets VS Everything and Paint and Hide!.
HUSH: They can hear rose +24 and +1 Slinky Escape +18, while Lanterns -28, Rush To The Vet! -26 and ScootX -21 fell.
Games under 15 days hold a median percentile of 70 against 48 at 15–42 days.
patterns: Recently updated games consistently rank higher among games of the same age (H-uc-012 at 70%); games idle 5 days or more sit at the bottom.
Server-wide products go with lower positions among games of the same age (within-age -0.40), so a new test is added. Build loops (-0.44) and rebirth mechanics (-0.43) also go with lower positions.
Everyday-life roleplay mechanics tend to go with higher positions (r=+0.39), consistent with H-uc-031.
Sound-based horror (DONT SPLASH, It Hears The Water, HUSH) is a visible cluster this week. Halloween is a confounder for every horror effect.

outliers.name: Steel Fighters
outliers.note: A build-and-rebirth collect game with 167 products and auto-play passes ranks near the top, against the build, rebirth and auto-pass patterns; fresh daily updates may outweigh them.

outliers.name: [🎃] Bike Universe
outliers.note: At 25 days it sits #2, above the age-band norm; its riding-for-cash loop and early Most Popular entry suggest a real breakout rather than novelty.

summary: Games pull players first and monetize later: the youngest games lead Top Trending and Up-and-Coming, while Top Earning efficiency rises from the 23rd percentile at 15–42 days to the 58th past a year.
Frequent updates help everywhere: days since update goes with worse results on Most Popular, Top Trending and Up-and-Coming at once.
Launch lean, deepen later: many passes, generic 2x passes and server-wide products go with weaker breakout, while higher prices and more passes go with efficiency in older games.
Horror with a single rule (anomaly spotting, sound-hunting monsters) and riding sims (bikes, scooters, rally) are this week's breakout clusters. Halloween is a confounder for the horror lift.
progressions: tt→mp stays the most common transition (84 entries, median 2 days), followed by uc→tt (83, 2 days) and te→tt (58, 7 days).
uc→te (51, 4 days) and uc→mp (49, 4 days) show breakouts reaching revenue and dominance within a week, while tt→uc stays at 1, so games still appear on Up-and-Coming first.
